item.description:

Heavy rain is expected, with total rainfall amounts of 40 to 60 mm. Rain will spread eastward through Saskatchewan today. Rain will continue through Saturday. Rain will be mixed with wet snow at times Saturday before changing over to snow Saturday night. Snow will end before Sunday. Water will likely pool on roads and in low-lying areas. Local utility outages are possible. Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to SKstorm@ec.gc.ca, call 1-800-239-0484 or post reports on social media using SKStorm.

item.title: Labour Mobility for Licensed Workers
item.description:
Labour Mobility for Licensed Workers jessicahughes Thu, 10/08/2026 - 09:51

PEI supports the movement of qualified workers across Canada through labour mobility provisions.

If you are certified in a regulated occupation in another Canadian province or territory, you may be eligible to have your credentials recognized in PEI without additional training, examinations, or work experience requirements.

The Canadian Free Trade Agreement (CFTA) supports labour mobility across Canada. Under Chapter 7 of the CFTA, workers certified by a regulator in one Canadian jurisdiction should generally be recognized by regulators in other jurisdictions.

Exceptions in PEI

PEI currently has approved exceptions for the following occupations:

  • Lawyer
  • Social Worker

Individuals in these occupations may need to demonstrate that they meet PEI-specific requirements before receiving certification.

For more information about labour mobility in Canada, please visit workersmobility.ca.

How do I Apply under Labour Mobility?

If you are certified in another Canadian province or territory:

Step 1

Find the regulatory body responsible for your profession in PEI.

Step 2

Submit a labour mobility application following the regulator's requirements. As part of the application process, regulators may request supporting information or documentation, including, but not limited to:

  • Proof of certification or licensure
  • Information on practice limitations, restrictions or conditions
  • Evidence of good character and professional standing
  • Demonstration of jurisdiction specific knowledge required for practice in PEI

Step 3

Once the regulator receives a complete application, a certification decision must be made within 30 calendar days.

Interprovincial Trade and Mobility Act (ITMA)

The Interprovincial Trade and Mobility Act and its regulations support faster labour mobility decisions for eligible professionals from reciprocal Canadian jurisdictions.

For eligible applications, regulatory bodies must make a decision within 10 days of receiving a complete application.

This streamlined process helps qualified professionals enter the PEI workforce more quickly.

Learn more: Interprovincial Trade and Mobility Act | Government of Prince Edward Island

item.title: Working in PEI with International Credentials
item.description:
Working in PEI with International Credentials jessicahughes Thu, 10/08/2026 - 09:36

If you completed your education or training outside Canada and want to work in a regulated occupation in Prince Edward Island, you will likely need to have your qualifications assessed before you can become licensed.

Foreign Credential Recognition (FCR) is the process used to determine whether education, skills, and work experience obtained outside Canada meet Canadian licensing requirements.

The credential recognition process varies depending on the occupation and the regulatory body responsible for licensing. The process may:

  • Require an assessment of your education, training, and work experience.
  • Include examinations, language proficiency testing, or additional training.
  • Involve application, assessment, and licensing fees.
  • Take several months or longer to complete, depending on the profession and individual circumstances.

Before you apply

Before applying for a license, you should:

  • Identify whether your occupation is regulated in PEI.
  • Contact the appropriate regulatory body to understand its licensing requirements.
  • Gather any required documents, such as transcripts, proof of identity, employment records, or professional certifications.

We encourage you to begin the credential recognition process before arriving in PEI whenever possible.

The Canadian Information Centre for International Credentials (CICIC) 

Learn more about the steps you may need to take to work in Canada.

item.title: Regulated Occupations
item.description:
Regulated Occupations jessicahughes Thu, 10/08/2026 - 09:24

Regulated occupations include professions and trades that are governed by legislation to protect public health, safety, and consumer interests.

To work in a regulated occupation in PEI, you must apply for certification or licensure through the appropriate regulatory body.

What Is a Regulatory Body?

A regulatory body (or regulator) is a government-approved organization responsible for governing a profession or trade.

Only individuals who meet the regulator's requirements can legally practice a regulated occupation in PEI.

Find Your Regulatory Body

Search the list of regulated occupations below to identify the regulatory body responsible for your profession and learn how to apply for registration in PEI.

Trades

Some trades in PEI are designated as certified compulsory. To legally work in a certified compulsory trade, you must either be:

  • A registered apprentice
  • The holder of a Certificate of Qualification

PEI’s certified compulsory trades are:

  • Automotive Service Technician
  • Construction Electrician
  • Plumber
  • Steamfitter / Pipefitter

For more information about designated trades, apprenticeship, and certification requirements, visit: Designated Trades in PEI | Government of Prince Edward Island
